assertions: retry after writer unlock preserves calls and bootstraps registry

approved_invariants: Transactional authority barrier fences old READ COMMITTED and REPEATABLE READ writers.
Post-barrier compatible capture persists durable admissions and never falls back to the local sequence.
Corporate ID/token reservations are unique and recovered using original operation/source identities.
Historical IDs, frozen payloads, hashes, outbox, quarantines and receipts remain preserved.
Unknown commits and remote outages keep durable evidence and recover forward without another UUID.
Schema/authority incompatibility blocks progress; quarantine remains a separate authorized selective operation.
conditions_blocking_real_activation: DBA approval of corporate 001, exact real schema/version/function ownership and role privileges; no unknown partial namespace.
Inventory and homologation of every corporate writer, including independent generators, UPSERT/COPY/functions/replication; free-ID writes can work while reserved/used-ID attempts reject.
Approved bootstrap lock window and capacity assessment for actual history, registry indexes, WAL, int32 and durable admissions storage.
Approved Dokploy admin image/container, bindings, CA/TLS mounts, secret-file handling and connectivity from the actual psql execution environment.
Previous validated completed reversion and intact quarantine, protected new generation, reviewed digest and explicit barrier/activation authorization.
Full batch registration, persisted active evidence, remaining-pending verification and separate delivery recovery/resume authorization.
Resolution of prior global test/typecheck acceptance failures to meet the complete PRD.
limits: No real production, WAN, OLOS retention or multi-million-row benchmark executed.
Synthetic tests do not homologate external writers or real Dokploy/DBA grants.
Owner/superuser can deliberately bypass database guards; actual roles require DBA review.
Old rejected nextval attempts can burn sequence values without creating persisted assignments.
After the barrier, only forward recovery with the same generation and a compatible binary is supported.
No new report/ingestion features, scheduler or second worker introduced.
